newsitem.title: LEBANON: Lebanon rejects bids for 35,000 tonnes wheat.
newsitem.headline: Lebanon rejects bids for 35,000 tonnes wheat.

text.p: Lebanon's economy ministry said it rejected on Tuesday all bids by local agents of international grain companies for the purchase on its behalf of 35,000 tonnes of hard U.S. wheat.

An official of the Office of Cereals and Sugar Beet said that seven local firms submitted bids for the purchase of 35,000 tonnes of hard red winter wheat on behalf of the ministry, with prices ranging from $203 to $207 per tonne.

"Seven firms took part in the tender but all the bids were rejected. The prices were deemed by the minister to be unsuitable especially as Egypt bought wheat yesterday at $167 per tonne," the official told Reuters.
The cereals office is part of the economy ministry.

The economy ministry invited the bids on February 7 saying the wheat was for March 15-31 shipment CIF to Beirut port silos. On January 8 the ministry said it was planning to buy 50,000 tonnes of U.S. hard wheat later in the month but it never invited tenders.
Lebanon has yearly wheat requirements of 400,000 tonnes.

The economy ministry periodically invites international grain companies or their Beirut agents to tender to buy wheat on the international markets on behalf of the Lebanese government. Local firms also make purchases for the private sector.
